rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The moderate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Change only gradient duration to measure how the crowded early cluster and marginal later pair respond to slope. This establishes whether a shallower gradient can resolve the critical pairs before adjusting temperature or trimming the solvent window.

Test temperature selectivity against injection 1 while retaining its fast gradient. Higher temperature may separate the crowded early cluster and shorten late retention without the time penalty of the shallower gradient.

Combine the favorable selectivity at 60 C with a shallower gradient to improve the sole remaining critical pair. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, allowing a fully resolved run to reach the maximum CRF.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so test a steeper gradient at the favorable temperature. This will reveal whether its resolution improves enough before the neighboring pair becomes limiting.

Slope changes alone have not resolved the remaining pair, so shift the starting organic fraction to probe solvent-window selectivity. Keep 60 C and a moderate gradient duration, while checking that the earliest peak remains retained.
Injection 6 reached the maximum CRF; shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Its critical pairs have limited headroom, so retain injection 6 as the fallback.

Narrow the gradient window to recover the small resolution deficits in injection 7 while keeping the shorter programmed gradient. The last peak should still elute within the gradient, with a faster fully resolved separation than injection 6.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction can shorten the fully resolved method while improving the limiting pair's selectivity. Monitor the early cluster closely because reduced initial retention may compress its other separations.

Return to 60 C and test a gradient slope between those of injections 7 and 8, targeting the resolution boundary. The narrower solvent window should keep the last peak within the gradient and may slightly shorten the fastest fully resolved separation.

Explore the opposite temperature extreme for a different elution order that might resolve the early cluster with a faster gradient. Retain injection 8 as the fully resolved benchmark; injection 11's rounded CRF masks a pair still below 1.5.
